Says whether a texture is completely loaded, without waiting for it. With [AsyncLoading](AsyncLoading) on, [LoadTexture](LoadTexture) returns while the picture is still being decoded on another thread, and this is 1 once that is done and the texture is on the graphics card. Calling it also finishes the loading when it is done, so a loop that waits for it costs nothing. Without asynchronous loading every texture is ready as soon as [LoadTexture](LoadTexture) returns, so this is always 1. Using the texture, for example with [EntityTexture](EntityTexture) and [RenderWorld](RenderWorld), [TextureWidth](TextureWidth) or [TextureBuffer](TextureBuffer), never needs this call: it waits for the loading by itself.

This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the originals have no asynchronous loading.
@param texture  The texture to ask about.
@returns 1 if the texture is loaded, and 0 if it is still loading or does not exist.
